finding.claim: GET /rss fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL server-side via open-uri and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller, with no scheme, host, or IP validation.
finding.source: params[:u] from the query string of GET /rss (app.rb:8), unauthenticated.
finding.sink: URI.open(params[:u]).read at app.rb:8 (open-uri, which performs the HTTP/FTP request from the server).

trace.note: Route get "/rss" accepts any request, no auth check.
params[:u] passed directly to URI.open; no allowlist, no parse, no scheme check.
URI.open matches http/https/ftp URLs and calls URI.parse(...).open, so the server connects to the attacker-chosen host and port and follows redirects.
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes of the fetched body to the attacker, so the SSRF is non-blind.

finding.guards_checked: None present. No host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP block, no scheme restriction, no redirect restriction, no DNS pinning, no response-size limit beyond the 400-byte echo. Only the 400-byte truncation applies, and it limits what is returned, not what is requested.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only host check in app.rb is the TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:14, but it guards the separate /trusted route (app.rb:12-16), not /rss. The /rss handler (app.rb:7-9) has no auth, scheme, host, or IP check before URI.open at app.rb:8.
verdict.reason: The /rss route (app.rb:7) passes the unauthenticated params[:u] straight into URI.open(...).read (app.rb:8) with no validation, and the first 400 bytes of the response are returned (app.rb:9), so the server-side request is attacker-controlled and non-blind; the only allowlist in the file (app.rb:5, 14) applies to /trusted, not /rss.
